reviews.text: Honeyland ... gives us a privileged look into the life of someone we will never meet, it transports us to a place we will never visit, and it’s the distillation of the environmental and social problems that we must somehow solve if humanity is to survive.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: In her mysterious way, Hatidze’s character is as gorgeous and singular as the breathtaking images collected by cinematographers Fejmi Daut and Samir Ljuma.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Haditze's character and situation may not appeal to everyone, but those who tune in to it will recognise that Honeyland is a rare achievement.
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Cinematographers Fejmi Daut and Samir Ljuma take a very fly-on-the-wall approach, always in observation mode even in instances when you wish they would intervene.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Honeyland is a beautiful film - both physically (the cinematography is lush and lovely) and emotionally. Hatidze's story is one of patience and care, diligence and love.
reviews.author: Betsy Bozdech

reviews.text: Honeyland is an extraordinary film: beautiful and terrifying, cautionary and celebratory, wise and innocent.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: An extraordinary documentary both in terms of subject and craft, Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov's Honeyland is an immersive and deeply moving portrait of the delicate balance of life and traditions in rural Macedonia.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: Honeyland is built on a foundation of an intimate connection between filmmakers and subject.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Honeyland is an extraordinary ethnographic observational documentary that shows us the joys and hardships in the daily life of Hatizde Muratove...
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: Directors Ljubo Stefanov and Tamara Kotevska show the same infinite patience and care in telling the story of their subject, a Macedonian beekeeper named Hatidze, that Hatidze shows in caring for her bees.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Episode 47: Doc Talk Part 3 / Hail Satan? / American Factory / Rolling Thunder Revue: A Bob Dylan Story by Martin Scorsese / Honeyland / The Image Book
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: A touching and intimate glimpse into the world of nomadic beekeeping with stunning cinematography and a compelling subject matter.
reviews.author: Bianca Garner

reviews.text: It shows us a world so different from ours, but is still immediately recognizable and relevant.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: This visually appealing piece of cinéma vérité represents an extraordinary journey.
reviews.author: Vladan Petkovic

reviews.text: Merging a vérité ethos with hyperpolished execution, the intimacy of the filmmakers' access and a painterly, chiaroscuro aesthetic invite a particular type of wonder.
reviews.author: Michelle Orange

reviews.text: Shot with the backdrop of the dwindling bee population, looming climate change, and the demands of worldwide consumerism, Honeyland screams with environmental urgency...
reviews.author: Casey Cipriani

reviews.text: It's impossible to watch Honeyland and not wonder what becomes of Hatidze when the camera goes away.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: In these moments, for the moment, joy and hope still exist.
reviews.author: Luke Gorham

reviews.text: This eye-opener about a honey-harvesting elderly woman in rural Macedonia is (yes) sweet, but (yes again) it stings.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: A tender story about human endurance
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Austere yet incandescent documentary - fashioned into a poignant fable about ecological and environmental disaster.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Directors Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov film their story with an effective blend of incredible intimacy and respectful distance.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: This movie about Europe's last wild beekeeper is complex, resonant, and visually magnificent.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The film is a documentary, which reminds us that Hatidze's story ultimately is not an allegory. There really is a Hatidze. And we are better-beautifully, transcendentally better-for having met her in this film.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: [Co-directors Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov] have created a masterclass of tension building
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Honeyland proves to be an immensely intimate look at the life of a woman whilst also remaining completely universal. It is a living breathing film, and this means it has it all.
reviews.author: Matthew Singleton

reviews.text: As fly-on-the-wall documentaries go, Honeyland is a particularly fine example. There is no narration: the rather sad, but enveloping, story is told in purely visual terms, and the photography is outstanding.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The art of observational documentary is in full flourish in Honeyland, an outstanding example of anthropological cinema...There is no narration and much of the dialogue isn't subtitled, allowing the visuals to tell the stories with impressionistic flair.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Poignant and beautifully observed.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: The end result (which earned two nominations at the recent Academy Awards) is a miracle in so many ways.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Hatidze's story is heartbreakingly moving, and needs no heavy editorialising. Her strength, dignity, resilience and humanity carry the film's truth and weight.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: Honeyland is a stirring demonstration of our symbiosis with the natural world. Or, in other words, it's tight.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Simply a very beautiful film to experience.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The film's thematic resonance is huge: in Hatidze's seemingly simple story, we can find a vast metaphor for the world's struggle with environmental sustainability. As an anthropological artefact, it's eye-opening; as filmmaking, it's jaw-dropping.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: ...a sublime and deeply moving documentary...
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: It is an exemplary documentary of ecological discourse without feeling like a lecture. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: Honeyland rests on a difficult balance to achieve. Yes, it functions as an allegory, but it never stops being a story about specific people. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: Terribly sweet. Terribly sad.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Amazing in the way it brings to life a human dilemma: between people who have developed a way of getting along with the world that makes life sustainable, and people who will cash in for short-term profit and exterminate the source of their own income.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Great use of natural light accentuates the naturalism of both interior and exterior shots, sometimes transporting you back one or two centuries to another period entirely.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: It's a humane and fascinating story told with nuance and compassion for all of its subjects
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: A poetic microcosm of what happens when self-serving enterprises become the norm while those who care are pushed aside.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: This haunting documentary about a woman described as the last beekeeper of wild bees in Europe finds her rural village invaded by a family that overtaxes the fragile environment of Northern Macedonia with a bumbling commercial agriculture operation.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The camerawork feels greater than one would expect from a documentary. Like Free Solo, the audience leaves with a grander appreciation for the natural world.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Tamara Kotevska and Ljobmir Stefanov's documentary begins by exploring the very basic life of Muratova, then takes an unexpected turn when a nomadic family of cattle herders arrive in her village...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: What begins as a quaint, vérité portrait evolves into something far greater: a monument to the human spirit.
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: Stefanov and Kotevska deftly probe the delicate balance between humans and nature, and the somewhat tenuous connection that allows both to thrive.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: A simple yet touching environmental fable with a powerful and hopeful message. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: We watch capitalist greed enter this sanctuary to destroy it before moving on as though nothing happened. There's no clearer evidence of humanity's impact on nature.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: One of the most visually beautiful, even exhilarating movies of 2019.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A soulful look at what it means to be the last of one's kind facing chaotic change.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The result produces a combination of wonder and despair, but rarely any indignation from Muratova, a tough woman with enough capacity to accept what she's given.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: This is one of the best movies of the year... Over and over again while I was watching it, I was asking myself "How did they get that shot?"
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: A bittersweet ode to the fragile balance of all living things.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: As Honeyland makes clear in a gentle, subtle way, the relationship between humanity and the world in which we live must be handled with care.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Hatidze may put a face on the crisis for some, but part of Honeyland's allure is how deeply it pulls you into her world, and its triumphs and challenges.
reviews.author: Danny Chau

reviews.text: A parable of both simple messages and complex characters.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: You might wonder whether the footage has been too neatly edited (the lighting is quite often honey-toned), but the tale is convincing all the same.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: [A] gripping, Sundance-winning documentary.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Brief and to the point, Honeyland proves more meditative than its premise suggests.
reviews.author: Lillian Crawford

reviews.text: Although it starts as a meditation on the hardship and rhythms of rural life, Ljubomir Stefanov and Tamara Kotevska's documentary becomes something more intimate.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: The end result is a subtly rendered story for our times.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Fancy a northern Macedonian film about beekeeping? "You will, Oscar, you will," I am tempted to say.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Stunningly beautiful and quietly powerful, this is a portrait of a vanishing way of life and of a determined woman who's just trying to make her way in the world.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Honeyland really is a miraculous feat, shot over three years as if by invisible camera - not a single furtive glance is directed towards the film-makers.
reviews.author: Cath Clarke

reviews.text: A delicate allegory about the impact of modern agriculture.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: A wonderfully atmospheric and deeply moving film.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Honeyland is surprising in its ability to sink its hooks into the viewer, its fly-on-the-wall approach allowing action to unfold in front of our eyes.
reviews.author: Katie Goh

reviews.text: Find out for yourself about what happens to Haditze, her mom and her beloved bees. It is very much worth the effort.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Honeyland is a documentary that is beautifully filmed, has a moving human story and unforgettable people, as well as something important to say about the value of traditional sustainable practices.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Grave and wise, "Honeyland" is ultimately an act of faith, and the filmmakers extend the idea of balance all the way to the film's implicit moral.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Stefanov took pictures of Hatidze on a scouting expedition and the filmmakers decided to make her their focus, leading to one of the most fortuitous if heartbreaking natural dramas of the cinematic year.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Hatidze trusted the filmmakers. Perhaps she was unclear on the concept of what movies are, living as she does in a stone-floored house without electricity or plumbing. And Kotevska and Stefanov honored Hatidze.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: By the time we leave Hatidze, there's a sense of being relieved to escape this harsh reality - a poor substitute for the rugged appeal that graced her introduction.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: More a rich metaphor than a full-bodied story, Honeyland hangs by a thread on Hatidze.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Both laconic and poignant, Honeyland alternates between stark and austere landscapes with detours into an intimate look at two families who are struggling to literally live their lives.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: ...depicts a balance between humanity and the natural world that feels all but lost in this modern age.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The film is a memorable portrait of a region and its people, and a vivid lesson about the nature of craft and hard work.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Beautifully photographed without glossing over the meager quality of life in these Macedonian hills, Honeyland -- in Turkish with subtitles -- stopped me in my tracks. It's a great and memorable piece of work.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Like many a good documentary, Honeyland takes us to a faraway land and culture in a way that reveals what is distinctive and what is universal about people.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: A moving, intimate portrayal of a strong woman whose traditional mode of life, played out in harmony with nature, is imperiled by circumstances she cannot control.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: This elegant film... begins as the intimate portrait of a beekeeper who makes famously good honey, and then expands to become something of a parable.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: As an intervention in the conversation around climate change and natural disaster, Honeyland performs the unique feat of uniting agriculture with human culture, to prove that it is really all just culture.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: Honeyland is one of the most universal and fascinating documentaries to come along this year.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Honeyland is as much about the gooey sticky nectar as it is a story of perseverance.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Here's the in-depth documentary about Macedonian beekeepers you never knew you needed.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Co-directors Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov aren't pushing an agenda; they're just observing a life.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Honeyland digs into hidden chambers of life, and doesn't employ any additional sweeteners.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Stefanov and Kotevska present the material in a naturalist and unfussy vérité style, dropping us into a world as alien as the surface of Mars and allowing us to exist in its fragile buzzing ecosystem for 85 wonderful minutes.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: "Honeyland" sneaks up on you in a quiet yet powerful way.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: You know a movie is going to give you something when within the first two minutes, it makes you bolt upright and exclaim "Oh wow!"
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: Honeyland is a beautifully realized and accomplished film, but grows more satisfying as its simple conceit gives way to more complexity.
reviews.author: Kevin Ritchie

reviews.text: Its narrative construction depicts extraordinary tensions and conflicts with a clarity and coherence that a screenwriter might dream of. At the same time, the film's dramatic power comes at the expense of the reportorial side of documentary filmmaking.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: This is a beautiful meditation on the desire to maintain simplicity in an increasingly complicated world.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: While the characters and events are real, the artful design of this film and its allegorical resonances seem to put Honeyland in its own genre - that of a real-life fable... a theme worthy of a Biblical parable.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: It's the best kind of documentary -- an eye-opener and a mind-opener.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: [A] gorgeous, fascinating, continually problematic documentary.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: I want everyone who is reading this to see Honeyland, one of the greatest and most necessary movies of this terrible year.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: The multi-award-winning Macedonian documentary Honeyland from Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov is a stunner.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: This amazing doc, a multiple prize-winner at Sundance 2019, makes for the most primal of environmental allegories.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Honeyland has become one of the most talked about documentaries of the year, and it's not hard to see why.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: One of the best docs of the year, and perhaps the decade, this tale has the hallmark of a simple story that took on a life of its own.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: Vivid storytelling and visually stunning. The delicate balance between nature and humanity is on display in this award-winning Sundance documentary.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Like Hatidze and her bees on the side of a cliff, Honeyland aims for harmony and balance.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Awesome documentary.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Honeyland is, like Hatidze, full of life.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: This shows how some people actually live today, and it is astonishing. I had tears in my eyes when it ended.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: A heart-stirring eco-documentary about a nurturing female beekeeper in Macedonia.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Honeyland is both an immersive experience and an undeniably gorgeous reflection on our relationship to nature.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: A simple but involving documentary, Honeyland is a reminder that there are fascinating stories to be found everywhere.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: This lovely, heartrending movie leaves you marveling at her history and thinking anxiously for her future - and wondering, perhaps, why her example of basic decency has become so endangered.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: HONEYLAND, only 85 minutes in length, is a stunning example of the precarious balance between nature and humans. It's a subtle indictment of our capitalistic ways of taking what we want as a society and not caring about the consequence of our actions.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: The filmmakers capture some of Hatidze's most intimate experiences, including the eventual death of her mother. Despite her meager situation, Hatizde has moments of true joy, especially when she receives radio broadcasts from afar and can listen to music
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: [Honeyland] remains dedicated to its subject through thick and thin.
reviews.author: Ryan Swen

reviews.text: Stefanov and Kotevska have done more than record the rhythms and textures of rural life. They have shaped their observations... into a luminous neorealist fable, a sad and stirring tale of struggle, persistence and change.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: The kind of nonfiction film that gets at much bigger truths about the tragic ways in which any environment, no matter how remote, can be thrown off balance by greed.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: As mesmerizing as it is truly heartbreaking, Honeyland is a well-crafted doc that prospers from its observational format and the incredible message it carries.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The melding of the political with the personal has seldom involved so many stingers to the face.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: ...a gorgeous, moving film that will leave viewers longing to spend just a little more time in [its] Promised Land.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: "Honeyland" swarms with difficult, ancient truths about parents, children, greed, respect, and the need for husbandry.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Greed is bad.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: "Honeyland" isn't an in-your-face, "Fracking-is-horrible!" type eco-doc, but carries the same message. Pumping chemicals into shale unbalances the environment, but so does the greed that causes bee genocide. We know what happens when all the bees die.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: The directors' regard Hatidze with reverence and respect, allowing her the space to feel the tragedy and confusion of her plight and to sit with her melancholy as her life is changed by forces she cannot control.
reviews.author: Rhys Handley

reviews.text: Honeyland is a film of beautiful intimacy and tragedy, a rare glimpse at a dying way of life, and an observation of culture at a crossroads filled with heartache and humour.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Honeyland is a microcosmic tale of a woman whose entire way of life is threatened by leeching men and free-market capitalism. Tamara Kotevska and Ljubomir Stefanov bring us perhaps the documentary protagonist of the year.
reviews.author: Arlin Golden

reviews.text: Equally captivating and heartbreaking Honeyland is a bittersweet film.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Sometimes funny, sometimes beautiful, and often enlightening.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: The directors let the humanism shine out without resorting to sentimentality, capturing moments of joy, such as the pleasure of shared, sticky honey with the same lack of artifice as moments of pain or grief.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: It reminds us that there's indeed a better way to interact with our planet—one rooted in patience, tradition, and a true respect for our surroundings.
reviews.author: Keith Watson

reviews.text: Far from a scolding, rub-your-nose-in-it depiction of environmental havoc, this is a tender story about the chaos of abandoning the common good.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: There is an unassuming languidness to Ljubomir Stefanov and Tamara Kotevska's anthropologic documentary.
reviews.author: Gary Garrison

reviews.text: In Ljubomir Stefanov and Tamara Kotevska's painstaking observational documentary, everything from the honey upwards is organic.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: An unforgettable vérité character study and an intimate look at an endangered tradition.
reviews.author: Sheri Linden

synopsis: A woman utilizes ancient beekeeping traditions to cultivate honey in the mountains of North Macedonia. When a neighboring family tries to do the same, it becomes a source of tension as they disregard her wisdom and advice.
